question: How many higher education institutions exist?
Must be a degree-granting body with an innovation function
rule: universities + colleges; standalone diploma institutes excluded (no innovation mandate)
note: Stand-alone institutions (12,002) are polytechnics, teacher-training and nursing institutes at diploma level. They have no IIC and no NIRF Innovation obligation. Excluding them removes 20% of the registered base.

question: Must have institutional internet, not just computers in a room
rule: universities x NKN share + colleges x NKN share
note: THE FINDING. Colleges have a computer centre in 88% of cases but institutional backbone connectivity in only 24%. A cloud product needs the backbone; the upper bound assumes computer-centre presence suffices.

question: Must demonstrably file an innovation return
rule: count of institutions that filed the Innovation category in 2025
note: The only filter with a directly observed count. Everything upstream of this is a proxy; this is 777 institutions that demonstrably did the work.

question: Must be able to afford the contract
rule: Rs 1.2L is 0.0063% of a NIT budget and 0.3% of the LOW end of the bounded private college revenue band
note: PASSES 100%. This filter excludes nobody, at either price. That is the Phase 5 result restated: affordability has never been the obstacle.

question: Must sit in a state whose startup ecosystem is functional
rule: exclude Emerging-tier states (7 of 34); institution counts by state are not public
note: BOUNDED, not measured. Seven states are Emerging-tier; their share of the 777 is not published. The 25% haircut is an analyst floor, not a measurement. Note the perverse case: Emerging states may be the BEST prospects because they have the most to gain and the least incumbent.

source: NIRF 2025 regional split; Startup India Tier 2/3 data
question: Must be reachable in the initial selling motion
rule: exclude the East (7.5% of filers, lowest concentration and most dispersed)
note: The East holds 7.5% of Innovation filers. Excluding it costs 7.5% of the market and is a distribution decision, not an economic one - the East is where relative improvement is easiest.
